summary: For production, deploy only known, tested package versions: the example installs pinned httpd RPM versions on RHEL 9 hosts with ansible.builtin.dnf state present and allow_downgrade: true, guarded by ansible_distribution and ansible_distribution_major_version; allow_downgrade downgrades newer installed versions.
questions: How do I install a specific RPM version with Ansible?
What does allow_downgrade do in ansible.builtin.dnf?
How do I pin httpd to a version on RHEL 9 with a playbook?
Only patch RHEL 9 hosts in a playbook

answer_card.title: Install specific RPM versions
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- name: Install specific RPM versions
  hosts: target_hosts
  gather_facts: true
  become: true
  vars:
    httpd_packages_rhel9:
      - httpd-2.4.53-11.el9_2.5
      - httpd-core-2.4.53-11.el9_2.5
      - httpd-tools-2.4.53-11.el9_2.5
  tasks:
    - name: Install httpd and dependencies
      ansible.builtin.dnf:
        name: '{{ httpd_packages_rhel9 }}'
        state: present
        allow_downgrade: true
      when:
        - ansible_distribution == "RedHat"
        - ansible_distribution_major_version == "9"
```
`allow_downgrade: true` downgrades a newer installed version to the listed one. Nothing changes if the versions are already in place or the host is not RHEL 9.
